definition.interpretation: The observed reward variance of 0.12 adheres to the hypothesis prediction (<= 0.15) for continuous goal representations. However, this result is inconclusive regarding the instrumental value of continuity as it lacks a comparative control baseline.
definition.limitations: The current protocol measures variance in isolation; it fails to demonstrate that continuous goal representations outperform non-continuous baselines in non-stationary environments.
definition.next_step: Define a comparative experimental protocol to measure relative reward variance between agents with and without continuous goal representations.

definition.cost: Minimal computational overhead; experiment design modification.
definition.next_experiment: Protocol comparing continuous vs. non-continuous agent performance in non-stationary environments.
definition.reason: Exp-continuity-variance-003 established a measurement threshold but not an effect size or comparative validity.
definition.stop_condition: Three consecutive failures to demonstrate a performance divergence between experimental and control agents.
definition.uncertainty: The instrumental advantage of continuity remains theoretically plausible but empirically unverified without a control group.
